To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transcription factors Satb and Ctip2 are required for axon growth from subtypes of projection neurons in the developing cerebral cortext.

(1) directed axon growth of cortical neurons occurs in the intermediate zone, prior to migration into cortical plate; (2) Satb2 and/or Ctip2 are expressed in the intermediate zone at this time; and (3) bi‐directional callosal and/or corticospinal projections are not correlated with Satb2 and CTIP co‐expression.
directed axon outgrowth from cortical neurons is initiated during migration through the intermediate zone, and that Satb2 and CTIP‐2 expression is correlated with this stage of development.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the early development of cortical axonal projection patterns.
the early stages of axon guidance and growth in the developing cerebral neocortex, and the transcription factors that may be involved in this process.

the early growth of axons from neurons of the developing cerebral cortex, and the relationship of this growth with expression of the transcription factors Satb1 (special AT‐r ich sequence binding protein 1) and Ctip1 (COUP-TF interacting protein 1).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
directed axon outgrowth is a feature of migrating neurons in the IZ and that the expression of the transcription factors Satb and Ctip2 correlates with the onset of directed axon outgrowths.
Satb2 and CTIP expression are required for the development of axon growth in callosal and CST neurons, respectively, but not the initiation of axon outgrowth.
Satb2/Ctrip2 co‐expression is not the cause for bi‐directional projections of early neocoical projection neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Satb2 and/or Ctip2 expression is necessary but not sufficient to specify callosal/corticospinal axonal projections.

the expression of SATB1 and SATB2 in the developing cerebral cortical neurons is correlated with the onset of directed axonal outgrowth, and this expression is maintained in the mature callosal neurons, but not in the corticospinal neurons.

the onset of directed axon projection from subtypes of projection neurons in the embryonic cerebral cortex correlates with the expression of specific transcription factors, and that these transcription factors may act as a molecular code to specify axonal projection pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of SatB2 and Ctip 2 is not sufficient to drive axon growth, but rather is likely to be involved in other aspects of cortical development.

Satb2 and CTIP‐2 expression correlates with the appearance of early axon growth in cortical projection neurons, and that these two transcription factors may play a role in the development of cortical projection neurons.
